verses.text: The fifth angel blew his trumpet. I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth. The star was given the key to the shaft of the bottomless pit.
He opened the shaft of the bottomless pit, and smoke rose out of it like smoke from a huge furnace. The sun and the sky were darkened by the smoke from the pit.
Out of the smoke came locusts onto the earth. They were given power to sting like scorpions on the earth.
They were told not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green plant, or any tree. They could only harm the people who did not have God's seal on their foreheads.
They were not allowed to kill those people, only to cause them pain for five months. The pain was like the pain of a scorpion sting.
In those days people will look for death but will not find it. They will want to die, but death will run away from them.
The locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads they wore something like gold crowns, and their faces looked like human faces.
Their hair was like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' teeth.
Their chests were covered with something like iron armour. The sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.
They had tails with stings like scorpions. In their tails they had power to hurt people for five months.
Their king was the angel of the bottomless pit. In Hebrew his name is Abaddon, and in Greek it is Apollyon, which means Destroyer.
The first terrible thing is past. Look, two more terrible things are still coming.
The sixth angel blew his trumpet. I heard a voice coming from the horns of the gold altar in front of God.
It said to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, "Set free the four angels who are tied up at the great river Euphrates!"
So the four angels were set free. They had been kept ready for this very hour, day, month, and year, to kill a third of all people.
I heard how many soldiers on horses there were: two hundred million.

In my vision I saw the horses and their riders. The riders wore armour that was fiery red, dark blue, and yellow like sulphur. The horses had heads like lions' heads, and fire, smoke, and sulphur came out of their mouths.
A third of all people were killed by these three disasters: the fire, the smoke, and the sulphur that came out of the horses' mouths.
The power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails. Their tails were like snakes, with heads that they used to hurt people.

The rest of the people, who were not killed by these disasters, still did not turn away from the things they had made with their own hands. They did not stop worshipping demons and idols made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, idols that cannot see, hear, or walk.
They also did not turn away from their murders, their witchcraft, their sexual sin, or their stealing.
